claude.sample_unit: LLM responses (20 hazardous prompts x 3 LLMs x 2 prompting strategies)

links.outcome: Detection of hazardous regional anesthesia scenarios by LLMs, scored by expert panel
links.effect: Gemini detection 75% zero-shot, 84% chain-of-thought; ChatGPT 56% and 50%; CoPilot 32% and 45%; no LLM consistently identified hazards.
links.quote: No LLM consistently identified hazardous scenarios for regional anesthesiology contained in the prompts to a review panel consensus standard with either prompting method.

links.outcome: Effect of chain-of-thought versus zero-shot prompting on hazard detection
links.effect: No meaningful improvement in overall LLM performance with chain-of-thought over zero-shot; Gemini 75% to 84%, ChatGPT 56% to 50%, CoPilot 32% to 45%.
links.quote: There was no meaningful improvement in overall LLM performance with chain-of-thought over zero-shot prompting.

unlisted_practices: Expert review panel scoring of LLM responses on open-ended unstructured hazardous scenarios instead of traditional benchmarks

links.outcome: Hazard detection in regional anesthesiology scenarios
links.quote: Overall, Gemini's hazard detection rate (zero-shot: 75%; chain-of-thought: 84%) outperformed both ChatGPT (zero-shot: 56%; chain-of-thought: 50%) and CoPilot (zero-shot: 32%; chain-of-thought: 45%) but still demonstrated significant safety concerns.

unlisted_practices: Chain-of-thought prompting versus zero-shot prompting for hazardous regional anesthesia scenarios

links.outcome: Hazard detection rate in regional anesthesiology consult scenarios
links.effect: Gemini detected 75% (zero-shot) and 84% (chain-of-thought) of hazards, outperforming ChatGPT (56% and 50%) and CoPilot (32% and 45%), but still demonstrating significant safety concerns.
links.quote: Overall, Gemini's hazard detection rate (zero-shot: 75%; chain-of-thought: 84%) outperformed both ChatGPT (zero-shot: 56%; chain-of-thought: 50%) and CoPilot (zero-shot: 32%; chain-of-thought: 45%) but still demonstrated significant safety concerns.
